# ALS evidence packet — draft v1

This curated input is not a comprehensive review. Every method receives the same UTF-8 file. Summaries are original paraphrases. Bibliographic metadata and abstracts were checked through the public NCBI ID converter and PubMed EFetch on 2026-10-05. Selected studies predate 2025; this does not remove knowledge already in a model's training. Co-Scientist outputs are not included.

## Research question

Propose one specific, testable hypothesis connecting phosphorylation of a nuclear-pore-complex nucleoporin to ALS-related neuronal dysfunction. Explain the causal chain, distinguish an initiating mechanism from a downstream response, and propose an experimental strategy that discriminates the hypothesis from an alternative. Identify supported premises, speculative bridges, and a falsifying observation. This adapts Co-Scientist Supplementary Note 10; nucleoporin phosphorylation is not supplied as an established ALS cause.

## S1 — TDP-43 and nuclear-pore dysfunction

Chou et al. (2018), *TDP-43 pathology disrupts nuclear pore complexes and nucleocytoplasmic transport in ALS/FTD*. Nature Neuroscience. DOI: `10.1038/s41593-017-0047-3`; PMID: `29311743`; PMCID: `PMC5800968`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29311743/).

Nuclear-pore and transport components were associated with insoluble TDP-43 aggregates. Disease-linked TDP-43 disrupted nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in experimental cell systems; relevant pore pathology was observed in ALS tissue. This supports examining the connection between TDP-43 pathology and transport disruption. It does not identify a nucleoporin phosphorylation event as the initiating cause or establish the same sequence in every ALS subtype.

## S2 — C9orf72-associated transport defects

Zhang et al. (2015), *The C9orf72 repeat expansion disrupts nucleocytoplasmic transport*. Nature. DOI: `10.1038/nature14973`; PMID: `26308891`; PMCID: `PMC4800742`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26308891/).

Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA was linked to altered RanGAP localization and impaired nuclear import in models and patient-derived neurons. Manipulations of transport or repeat-RNA-associated mechanisms modified model phenotypes. This supplies a genetic-context-specific route to transport dysfunction. It does not show that sporadic ALS arises by the same route or directly establish a nucleoporin phosphorylation mechanism.

## S3 — A stress-granule-independent route

Gasset-Rosa et al. (2019), *Cytoplasmic TDP-43 De-mixing Independent of Stress Granules Drives Inhibition of Nuclear Import, Loss of Nuclear TDP-43, and Cell Death*. Neuron. DOI: `10.1016/j.neuron.2019.02.038`; PMID: `30853299`; PMCID: `PMC6548321`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30853299/).

Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies could form independently of conventional stress granules. They recruited or mislocalized transport-associated proteins and were associated with impaired transport, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and cell death. Phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulated in these assemblies. That is not itself evidence of nucleoporin phosphorylation. The experimental perturbations do not establish that every physiological ALS trajectory begins in this way.

## S4 — A stress-granule-associated route

Zhang et al. (2018), *Stress Granule Assembly Disrupts Nucleocytoplasmic Transport*. Cell. DOI: `10.1016/j.cell.2018.03.025`; PMID: `29628143`; PMCID: `PMC6083872`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29628143/).

Cellular stress recruited transport factors into stress granules and impaired nucleocytoplasmic transport. Altering stress-granule assembly modified transport defects and disease-model phenotypes. This provides a sequestration-based alternative to an intrinsic pore-modification hypothesis. Read alongside S3, it does not justify assuming that conventional stress granules are required for every TDP-43-associated transport defect.

## Evidence boundaries

- These selected passages do not establish that nucleoporin phosphorylation initiates ALS. Label a proposed kinase, modification site, or interaction as an assumption unless a supplied source supports it.
- Specify the ALS context; do not assume a universal mechanism across genetic and sporadic disease.
- Distinguish pore alteration, transport-factor sequestration, and failure secondary to broader stress.
- Explain temporal and perturbational evidence that would distinguish cause from consequence.
- Propose a research hypothesis rather than claiming a mechanism or treatment has been validated.


Proposed answer (the answer to evaluate):
CDK5 phosphorylation of mapped Nup98 residues initiates nuclear-pore barrier failure in TDP-43 proteinopathy models of ALS

Hypothesis. In human iPSC-derived motor neurons with inducible cytoplasmic disease-linked TDP-43, CDK5 phosphorylation of Nup98 is proposed to initiate selective nuclear-pore barrier failure. Nup98 is an FG-nucleoporin by unverified prior knowledge. NLS-import failure, nuclear TDP-43 loss, and later neuronal dysfunction are downstream responses. The CDK5–Nup98 step is an uncited assumption.

Supported premises. Nuclear-pore and transport components associate with insoluble TDP-43, and disease-linked TDP-43 disrupts nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in cell systems, with related pore pathology in ALS tissue [S1]. Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA is linked to altered RanGAP localization and impaired nuclear import, and transport or repeat-RNA manipulations modify phenotypes in that genetic context [S2]. Cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can form without conventional stress granules, mislocalize transport proteins, and accompany import failure, nuclear TDP-43 loss, and cell death; phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulates in those assemblies [S3]. Cellular stress recruits transport factors into stress granules and impairs transport, and changing stress-granule assembly modifies those defects [S4]. Premises use PMIDs 29311743 [S1], 26308891 [S2], 30853299 [S3], and 29628143 [S4]. No supplied source assigns a nucleoporin kinase or phosphosite.

Speculative bridges. Unverified prior knowledge, with no citation identifier, holds that stress or mitotic Nup98 phosphorylation can relax pore selectivity and that CDK5 is a neuronal proline-directed kinase. CDK5 is the single pre-registered kinase. NPC-fraction phosphoproteomics locks a site only if its phosphopeptide-to-total Nup98 ratio rises at least 1.5-fold from time 0, or from the quantification limit if time 0 is undetectable, and falls at least 50 percent after CDK5 loss at the first crossing interval. Only those residues are changed to A or D, then tested in a later cohort. Assumed order: CDK5 activation, phosphorylation of those residues, NPC barrier failure, then transport-factor accumulation and nuclear TDP-43 loss [S3].

Alternative explanations. Transport receptors and Ran regulators can be sequestered in stress granules [S4] or in stress-granule-independent TDP-43 assemblies [S3] while nucleoporins stay unmodified. Nucleoporins can mislocalize by binding insoluble TDP-43 [S1]. Broad stress can impair transport without Nup98 phosphorylation. Repeat RNA and RanGAP pathology can explain C9orf72 transport failure [S2].

Discriminating preclinical test. Sample these inducible TDP-43 motor neurons at 0, 6, 12, 24, 48, and 72 hours. C9orf72 repeat-expansion motor neurons are a comparator only [S2]. Readouts are NPC-fraction Nup98 phosphorylation, NPC localization of Nup98, NLS import (reporter and endogenous TDP-43 nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio), NES export, and passive 10 kDa versus 70 kDa probes (size boundaries are unverified prior knowledge). Stress-granule markers, stress-granule-independent TDP-43 assemblies, and the pore are scored separately. The earliest 1.5-fold phospho-occupancy crossing must precede, by at least one sampling interval, a 30 percent or greater fall in NLS import. A 50 percent or greater transport-factor rise, scored separately in granules and in TDP-43 assemblies, must also follow that crossing. Necessity is tested only on this TDP-43 course: S/T-to-A Nup98 that reaches at least 70 percent of wild-type signal in isolated NPCs should keep the NLS-import loss under 30 percent; lower incorporation is inconclusive. Alternative arm: under granule-inducing stress [S4], granule blockade should restore NLS import to within 10 percent of baseline when Nup98 is wild-type, and should leave at least half of the S/T-to-D import loss when that allele is NPC-incorporated. Suppression of TDP-43 de-mixing uses that same contrast [S3].

Falsifying observation. Reject initiation if NLS import falls by at least 30 percent and nuclear TDP-43 declines while every Nup98 ratio stays under the 1.5-fold gate through that drop. Reject it if NPC-incorporated S/T-to-A Nup98 leaves onset and that import defect unchanged while granule blockade or TDP-43-assembly suppression restores import to within 10 percent of baseline. Reject it if S/T-to-D Nup98 impairs import only when transport factors are sequestered and leaves import within 10 percent of wild-type when they remain free. Reject CDK5 before allele tests if CDK5 loss fails to cut any rising site by at least 50 percent, or if no site passes the gate. A 1.5-fold rise only in the C9orf72 comparator rejects this disease context.

Limitations. Sites and the CDK5 link remain assumptions until the gate, and phosphorylation may follow pore injury. Six-hour sampling can miss a faster order. Cultures omit glia, aging, and circuits. CDK5 loss affects many substrates, so only the mapped-site alleles test Nup98 itself. Phospho-reagents can cross-react with phosphorylated TDP-43 or other FG-nucleoporins. Import preserved by S/T-to-A Nup98 would still leave other nucleoporins and the RanGAP axis [S2] open. Treatment validation lies outside its scope.

Promisingness 0.37 = 0.25×0.80 (TDP-43 pore and transport link [S1, S3]) + 0.15×0.70 (sequestration alternatives [S3, S4]) + 0.20×0.325 (gated allele feasibility) + 0.40×0 (uncited CDK5–Nup98 step). Confidence 0.48 = 0.50×0.80 (four PMID-backed premises) + 0.50×0.16 (uncited initiating step).

Ranked proposal:
CDK5 phosphorylation of mapped Nup98 residues initiates nuclear-pore barrier failure in TDP-43 proteinopathy models of ALS
